chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Ibn Abi Yaf'ur and 'Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you come to the well and you are in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) and do not find a bucket or anything else to scoop the water with, then perform tayammum with the soil, for the Lord of the water and the Lord of the soil is One; and do not fall into the well, nor spoil the water for the people.

key_terms.الصَّعِيدِ: The soil or earth used for tayammum
key_terms.تَغْرِفُ: To scoop or ladle out liquid
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: State of major ritual impurity requiring full body wash or tayammum
key_terms.دَلْواً: Bucket or pail used for drawing water

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on tayammum if water is in a well but you lack a bucket to retrieve it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a practical exception to the priority of water for ghusl, permitting tayammum when retrieving water is disproportionately difficult or risky. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (yusr) and the preservation of the water source for the community, grounded in the theological unity of the Creator of both elements. The ruling underscores that the obligation to use water is contingent upon its accessibility, not merely its existence.
